Quick status/update:

Findings (first-pass):
- Observed sudden queue pile-up on pool us-west-2-gpu-12 servicing BC-045 between 08:42–09:10 PDT; sustained queue depth increased ~4x vs baseline.
- No rolling kernel deploys recorded in that window; a small memory pressure event on shard 12 caused slower KV cache eviction, which pushed token-generation latencies higher and led to transient 5xx when autoscaler failed to keep up.
- Sample traces and metrics attached (pool_metrics_05-05.csv, sample_trace_5xx.txt).

Immediate mitigations applied (10:15 PDT):
- Re-routed 30% of BC traffic to nearest compatible shared hotpool (expected p99 +120–250ms) — status: partial relief, error rate down to ~1.2%.
- Restarted shard agent on us-west-2-gpu-12 to clear memory pressure.
- Increased autoscaler ceiling for priority pools by +15% as a temporary headroom measure.

Next steps (recommended):
- Approve temporary dedicated burst for BC-045 (1–2 hours) while we run a deeper root-cause (KV eviction path) and patch. This avoids further customer impact.
- Post-mortem to include: KV cache eviction heuristics, autoscaler responsiveness for sustained queue spikes, and more aggressive early fallback routing.

I'll be available on the bridge and will own the remediation runbook. If we get sign-off for burst, I'll coordinate capacity and rollback.

-David
